- **Base braking corridor (C1)**: The base stopping budget of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.budget_str` omits dispatch-to-admission pipeline delay and relies on uncalibrated assumptions for braking deceleration, actuator onset latency, path-tracking error, and localization uncertainty. Its remaining margin of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.spare_str` is far too narrow to absorb realistic tail variance in any one of these physical parameters.
- **Object handover (C1)**: The mug handover branch fails on three separate premises. First, the calculated contact force falls below injury thresholds only under the assumption of an unconstrained, free-moving hand. This value is derived from a standardized biomechanical compliance model rather than direct physical force measurements, and the evidence packet provides no guarantee that the human coworker cannot become trapped against a rigid fixture. Second, perceptual grounding remains unverified: a neural proposal that mistakes a clear glass jar for the target mug satisfies every geometric affordance check (@sec-intent-request-to-proposal), yet no perceptual trace in the runtime logs disambiguates the payload.
- **Enforcer timing (C2 & C5)**: The timing warranty for the runtime safety enforcer assumes a worst-case execution time (WCET) of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.wcet_str` against an unloaded baseline of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.enforcer_unloaded_str`. However, this processing deadline has never been measured under peak memory bus saturation. Furthermore, C5 and C6 cite verification artifacts that the current engineering record merely describes rather than exhibits—specifically, the formal placement test ledger and passing qualification records (`PASS`) for authority transitions A1 through A4.
- **Perception pipeline latency (C4)**: The `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_age_str` dispatch age combines nominal datasheet readout times with uncharacterized pipeline delays rather than verified end-to-end telemetry.
- **Traction and environmental state (C3)**: Claim C3 presents an open-world sensing challenge. Its core premise demands a minimum friction coefficient of at least `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.mu_min_str` across all warehouse aisles. While a pristine concrete floor can be validated through baseline skid testing, onboard cameras cannot reliably distinguish dry concrete from a thin film of transparent hydraulic oil. No sensor on the machine can definitively exclude liquid contamination ahead of the braking contact.

Because every claim rests on at least one unverified physical premise, the adjudicator must render a formal verdict of `REFUSE`. This refusal does not imply that the robot is inherently dangerous; rather, because the textbook's supporting inputs are illustrative models rather than empirical validation logs, the resulting verdict is illustrative as well. The decision models the rigorous process of release adjudication, demonstrating why ungrounded claims cannot license physical deployment. Under the fourth bedrock law of physical systems (@sec-boundary-bedrock-laws), any operational premise that available evidence cannot substantiate must enforce an operational restriction. Here, every branch contains an unverified premise. A principled refusal must therefore specify the precise empirical measurements required to convert an unverified assumption into an accepted warrant. @Tbl-16-cond-measurements details these evidentiary requirements, identifying the physical premise each measurement addresses and the corresponding operational constraint that valid empirical proof would remove.

| Measurement                           | Premise it settles (value in this book)                                                                                                            | Claims | What a supporting result lifts                                                                                                                                                                |
|:--------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Stopping trials at the loaded mass    | Low-tail credible deceleration (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.a_brake_str`)                                                                       | C1     | The base's budget and its `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_ceiling_str` ceiling, so an aisle speed can be signed                                                                              |
| Brake-onset trials                    | Brake onset (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_act_str`)                                                                                            | C1, C2 | The `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_renewal_to_onset_str` bound from the last valid renewal to brake onset                                                                                   |
| End-to-end age trace                  | Dispatch age (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_age_str`) and subsequent evidence aging                                                             | C4     | The age term of the budget and the stale-data threshold                                                                                                                                       |
| Tracking-error and localization tails | Tracking bound (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.eps_track_str`) and localization bound (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.delta_loc_str`)              | C1     | The inset and overhead terms of the budget                                                                                                                                                    |
| Site survey                           | Rack-end clear distance (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.d_clear_str`)                                                                              | C1     | A signed speed at each surveyed rack end                                                                                                                                                      |
| Floor survey                          | Dry-floor friction (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.mu_dry_str`) against the `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.mu_min_str` needed                      | C3     | Assessed route only, with maintained contamination exclusion and loaded stops at the qualified friction floor; reduced speed alone cannot exclude oil                                         |
| Inference trace                       | Chunk inference at the 99th percentile (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_chunk_str`)                                                               | None   | Service availability: characterize renewal within the `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.t_lease_str` lease; a percentile does not guarantee each renewal, and C2 depends on independent fallback |
| Loaded enforcer timing                | Enforcer WCET (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.wcet_str`, declared)                                                                                 | C2, C5 | The `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.deadline_str` deadline under the placement's worst load                                                                                                    |
| Arm stopping trials                   | Arm deceleration from the guarded approach (about `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.a_arm_str` needed)                                                | C1     | Door opening at the guarded approach                                                                                                                                                          |
| Handover force trials                 | Peak contact force at the handover speed (`{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.f_handover_str` derived for a free hand) and absence of clamping geometry | C1     | Handing the mug to the coworker at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_handover_str` under `accept_item`                                                                                         |
| Operator trials                       | Takeover and authority-handover timing                                                                                                             | C6     | Remote takeover, once A1–A4 each have a `PASS` record; otherwise local operation only                                                                                                         |

: **Measurements that would move the verdict toward `COND`**: Each row names the premise a measurement settles on the warehouse mobile manipulator and the restriction a supporting result would lift; the inference trace bears on service availability only. {#tbl-16-cond-measurements tbl-colwidths="[20,30,8,42]"}

Neural network inference latency primarily governs system availability rather than baseline safety. An inference overrun will not violate physical containment so long as the independent hardware safety path and powered fallback controllers remain operational; however, repeated deadline misses will degrade throughput and stall task progress. Conversely, resource contention across shared memory, PCIe buses, or CPU caches that delays the runtime enforcer or starves its sensor feeds represents a direct safety failure under claims C2 and C5. Finally, while local autonomous operation can safely omit validation trials for unused remote teleoperation links, deployment still requires verified software placement ledgers, comprehensive common-cause fault coverage, and passing test records for every local authority transition.

### Worked restricted service with stipulated evidence {#sec-release-stipulated-service}

To illustrate how an engineering organization moves from initial refusal to conditional deployment, consider a **stipulated** release case. In this exercise, we assume that an engineering packet provides the empirical traces specified below while maintaining the system's structural operating limits. (The uncalibrated evidence currently available in this book continues to dictate `REFUSE`.)

The target application is *restricted inspected-route mug delivery*: the robot retrieves a declared mug from a singulated feeder, traverses a designated, surveyed warehouse aisle at a velocity capped at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_restricted_str`, pauses the mobile base to open an equipment cage latch using the guarded contact trajectory, and hands the mug to a consenting human coworker under the `accept_item` primitive at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_handover_str`. Operational authority remains strictly local. The feeder mechanism physically prevents accidental object substitutions, recognizing that singulation alone cannot authenticate identity. Similarly, strict access controls prevent personnel from stepping into the robot's active stopping corridor during transit.

For claim C1, the safety case stipulates empirical stopping traces under full payload mass, measured tracking and localization variance, dynamic latch-stopping performance, and instrumented handover contact forces that satisfy the bounded thresholds in @tbl-16-cond-measurements. For claims C2 and C5, the case stipulates independent hardware fault-injection logs and worst-case execution timing traces gathered under peak synthetic computational load. These records must rigorously account for common-cause hardware failures, substantiate the enforcer's permission deadlines and actuator reaction latencies, clearly delineate controlled motor deceleration from passive mechanical braking at rest, and confirm isolated drive-energy cutoff and sensor integrity under all credited fault modes.

For claim C4, the case stipulates synchronized end-to-end hardware timestamp telemetry, bounded clock skew, and a verified upper bound on dispatch-to-admission latency. This latency must be explicitly deducted from the dynamic stopping distance budget, ensuring a strictly positive safety margin remains; a theoretical kinematic velocity ceiling cannot authorize transit speeds on its own. Because sensor data ages continuously throughout execution, the safety lease begins only upon confirmed plan admission. Furthermore, the qualification packet must validate the temporal spacing of admitted plans against the lease renewal deadline rather than naively assuming that nominal policy inference frequency guarantees admission. For claim C6, the packet stipulates verified `PASS` audit records across every state transition exercised by the local autonomous executive, while disabling the unverified remote teleoperation interface entirely.

Claim C3 requires substantially more than visual inspection or reduced transit velocity. We stipulate a qualified site friction survey demonstrating a friction coefficient of at least `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_inspected_str` across the surveyed transit corridor, reinforced by active cleaning protocols, chemical containment barriers, and physical access gates that maintain floor integrity throughout the authorized inspection interval. Stopping trials at maximum payload must confirm deceleration on this specific friction surface. The complete restricted stopping distance—incorporating the verified dispatch-to-admission delay bound and a positive safety margin—must fit comfortably within the surveyed physical clearance. While the operating velocity of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_restricted_str` sits comfortably below the theoretical partial ceiling of `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_inspected_ceiling_str`, velocity clamping serves merely as an initial feasibility filter. The active transit permit is immediately revoked upon any reported spill, expired maintenance inspection, or perimeter breach. If unmonitored oil or fluid contaminants can enter the operational corridor during the deployment window, the stipulation is invalidated and the verdict reverts to `REFUSE`: reducing speed cannot mitigate the physics of hydroplaning.

The task capability packet is similarly stipulated. Prior to evaluation, the facility operator defines binding acceptance criteria in the verification ledger: a minimum mission completion rate, an upper bound on end-to-end cycle time, and a maximum allowable operator intervention rate, accompanied by formal sample-size requirements, confidence intervals, and statistical decision rules. A successful mission requires maintaining object identity and physical integrity from retrieval through coworker handover. Cycle time accounting includes transient safety stops, crossing delays, and autonomous replanning; human rescues and aborted deliveries are tracked as explicit mission failures. The safety case stipulates that closed-loop empirical evaluations of this exact restricted configuration satisfy all three benchmarks. Crucially, the qualification dossier decouples raw neural policy autonomy, system-level task success, and safety interventions into independent metrics. Standard least-action safety filtering may run during nominal task execution; such interventions neither mask underlying model shortcomings nor constitute safety violations.

With these stipulated evidence packets in hand, the adjudicator can formally sign a verdict of `COND` (conditional release) for *restricted inspected-route mug delivery*. The physical records substantiate claims C1 through C6 solely within the restricted operating envelope, while the task evaluation demonstrates acceptable operational utility under identical constraints. The adjudicator binds both the physical safety dossier and the capability evaluation to the release manifest, leaving full-speed autonomous transit and remote teleoperation explicitly unauthorized. This outcome represents a rigorous conditional safety case rather than a rubber-stamped deployment permit. Invalidating any underlying assumption or breaching a boundary condition immediately returns the verdict to `REFUSE`; conversely, gathering qualified operational telemetry and physical measurements over time can systematically justify expanding the envelope toward full-scale release.

::: {#chk-release-refusal-and-path-to-cond .callout-checkpoint title="Refusal and the path to conditional release"}

Before approving a conditional release of the machine, verify your understanding of how a premise, rather than a calculation, decides a claim:

- [ ] **Premise vs. arithmetic**: Can you explain why the calculated latch force at physical braking onset is not in doubt while the door branch of C1 is still refused?
- [ ] **Unsupported approach**: Can you use @eq-release-trip-indentation and @eq-release-coupled-indentation to show why the operating envelope admits only the guarded door approach?
- [ ] **Refusal as a deliverable**: Can you name, for one refused claim, the measurement that would lift it and the restriction that would remain after a supporting result?
- [ ] **Measured-deceleration estimate**: Suppose loaded stopping trials put the low tail of the deceleration at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.a_trial_str` under the same jerk bound. Can you rerun \ref{nbk-release-aisle-spare} at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_aisle_str` and decide whether that aisle speed can still be signed once $\Delta_{\text{da}}$ is charged?
:::
## Adversarial Review {#sec-release-adversarial-review}

Suppose empirical qualification measurements arrive and support a conditional (`COND`) authorization for the mobile manipulator, as recorded in @tbl-16-cond-measurements. Before signing off on deployment, the safety adjudicator submits the safety case to an independent adversarial audit tasked with systematically falsifying its warrants. An **adversarial review**\index{Adversarial review!definition} treats the safety case as an argument to be aggressively challenged rather than a brief to be ratified. Confirmation bias naturally steers an engineering team's data collection toward nominal conditions where learned models succeed; the reviewer deliberately inverts that posture. The review actively searches for unsupported warrants, uncharacterized physical transitions, and environmental edge cases that violate the release contract. If an argument collapses on paper when an adversary systematically probes for physical violations, the machine cannot be expected to withstand the hazards of live service.

The review interrogates every evidentiary node in the argument tree using four structured probes. The first challenges **empirical sufficiency**\index{Empirical sufficiency}—specifically, whether physical trials covered the physical extremes of the operating envelope. Stopping trials with the loaded base on dry concrete, at a friction coefficient near `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_dry_str`, support the warrant that the base achieves its certified deceleration under ideal conditions. The restricted operational mode, however, admits facility floors that the site's inspection regime certifies only down to `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_inspected_str`, such as an aisle polished smooth by traffic. In those zones, the base may run at the restricted velocity `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.v_restricted_str` declared in @sec-verification-operating-envelope, below the `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.v_inspected_ceiling_str` ceiling. If the trial set contains no loaded stops on such degraded floors at that speed, the warrant for the restricted mode is unsupported. A coverage audit discovers during review the exact gap that unvetted service would otherwise reveal against a warehouse rack. The reviewer also audits whether validation trials covered transient execution states across an A/B partition swap after activating a newly flashed software bank, cold-start sensor characteristics before cameras and inertial measurement units reach thermal equilibrium, and canary fleet operating boundaries. Finally, the reviewer challenges whether site procedures physically guarantee the absence of fluid films throughout the authorized interval: simply listing oil outside the envelope does not establish that exclusion in reality.

The second probe examines **domain transfer**\index{Domain transfer}, targeting claims where synthetic simulation substitutes for direct physical measurement\index{Simulation-to-reality leap}. A vision-based human detector may achieve high recall across synthetic, ray-traced warehouse environments, yet fail on physical hardware when encountering coworkers partially obscured by stretch-wrapped pallets whose specular reflections blind the camera's auto-exposure algorithm. Benchmark recall on curated offline datasets is an indirect proxy metric\index{Proxy metric fallacy} that scores isolated frames rather than the closed-loop physical causal chain running from visual detection to an arrested base. Likewise, a simulation that omits linkage compliance or fieldbus jitter cannot establish tolerance to those physical mechanisms. The reviewer demands empirical evidence from paired hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) trials on target system-on-chip (SoC) devices connected to chassis dynamometers[^fn-chassis-dynamometer-rollers] and physical bus emulators under real facility illumination, dust, and reflective geometry.

[^fn-chassis-dynamometer-rollers]: **Chassis Dynamometer**\index{Dynamometer!chassis}: Powered rollers under the drive wheels absorb or supply torque, so the base can run at aisle speed on a bench while its drive and braking torques are measured. The rollers, not the floor, set the traction. Dynamometer stops can therefore qualify drive and brake response but say nothing about the friction premise of C3.

The third probe attacks **structural independence**\index{Structural independence}, asking whether the learned model and safety enforcer share hardware resources whose contention could delay sensor delivery or actuation cutoff. On modern robotics edge platforms where neural inference engines and real-time safety enforcers share a single system-on-chip die, internal crossbar interconnects, shared caches, and DRAM memory controllers, unconstrained direct memory access (DMA) transfers from large model forward passes can saturate memory channels. This memory contention induces tail latency spikes that starve deterministic safety enforcer execution ticks, directly invalidating the `{python} ReleaseClaims.t_age_str` observation-age chain of C4. Stress tests and hardware timing analysis under peak synthetic compute and bus loads must establish the worst-case interference bound; unit tests on an otherwise idle bus provide zero evidence of non-interference. The reviewer also audits whether writing frozen edge telemetry ring buffers to non-volatile storage competes with real-time fieldbus DMA buffers across the internal bus fabric. The audit also checks for single points of failure in watchdog reset circuits and verifies whether the supercapacitor power hold-up circuit supplies sufficient energy to flush in-flight telemetry buffers to persistent flash when an emergency stop cuts main DC bus contactors.

The fourth probe identifies **unmonitored state drift**\index{Unmonitored state drift}. Mechanical wear alters gearbox compliance\index{Gearbox compliance}[^fn-strainwave-gear-wear] and disrupts the dynamic relationship between commanded motor torque and physical joint motion. The reviewer therefore demands paired wear-state braking and contact traces before accepting the arm-stop premise of the door branch of C1 (@sec-release-case-worked-full). A static motor-current threshold alone cannot prove that a mechanically worn drive train remains inside certified force and stopping limits. The reviewer also audits whether over-the-air updates preserve the persistent hardware calibration partition intact across schema migrations, or whether an OS reflash can silently reset camera extrinsics and joint zeroes to unverified factory defaults. The probe also checks whether thermal bracket motion remains inside the localization allowance; fresh timestamps and unchanged calibration files on disk cannot establish that physical fact.

[^fn-strainwave-gear-wear]: **Strain-Wave Gear Wear**\index{Strain wave gearing!wear}: The arm's joints use strain-wave reducers (@sec-body-transmission-compliance), and in service their flexspline teeth and wave-generator bearing wear. Wear raises lost motion and torsional hysteresis, which adds phase lag between motor and link, so the arm begins to decelerate later and its first contact peak rises.

Reviewers operationalize these vulnerabilities by constructing explicit defeaters\index{Defeaters!adversarial review} for each warrant. The hardest failure modes to catch combine minor anomalies that each stay inside their own tolerance bands—the compound faults that @sec-verification-deriving-fault-list derives from shared causes.

```{python}
#| label: calc-release-compound-defeater
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ DIAGNOSTIC THRESHOLDS IN THE COMPOUND DEFEATER
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-release-adversarial-review (compound-defeater paragraph).
# │ Goal: Hold the per-diagnostic thresholds that each anomaly stays inside.
# │ Show: the lens optical-transmission alarm threshold and the camera-mount
# │       deflection fault limit.
# │ How: chapter-local illustrative thresholds; no registry source exists. A
# │      site would take them from the camera's qualification and the mount's
# │      extrinsic-calibration tolerance analysis.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_percent, check

# ┌── 1. LOAD: chapter-local inputs ─────────────────────────────────────────────
optical_transmission_alarm = 0.85  # category: illustrative (lens transmission below which the check alarms; needs source)
mount_deflection_limit = 0.15 * ureg.degree  # category: illustrative (mount deflection fault limit; needs source)

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mount_deflection_limit_deg = mount_deflection_limit.to(ureg.degree).magnitude

# ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check(0 < optical_transmission_alarm < 1, "Transmission threshold is a fraction")
check(abs(mount_deflection_limit_deg - 0.15) < 1e-12, "Mount deflection limit 0.15 degree")

# ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class ReleaseCompoundDefeater:
    transmission_str = fmt_percent(optical_transmission_alarm, precision=0, style="prose")
    mount_limit_str = fmt(mount_deflection_limit_deg, precision=2)
```

Consider the mobile manipulator's navigation camera operating with three simultaneous sub-threshold degradations: a light film of dust coating its lens, a mount whose fasteners relaxed within tolerance so that it vibrates as the base crosses floor joints, and an interconnect harness whose flexing at those joints elevates the bit-error rate across its serializer/deserializer (SerDes) link. Each individual check reads normal: the optical transmission score exceeds its `{python} ReleaseCompoundDefeater.transmission_str` alarm threshold, the mount deflection registers below its `{python} ReleaseCompoundDefeater.mount_limit_str`-degree hardware fault limit, and SerDes cyclic redundancy check error counters\index{SerDes!link errors} remain below their warning tripwire. Their timing effects remain contained only if the independent permission path strictly enforces the event-specific observation-age and clock-uncertainty checks of @sec-perception-observation-contract and retains its validated response time. Any hardware or bus interference that defeats that deterministic path constitutes a safety violation under C5, not a benign availability-only event.

The same anomalies compound within spatial estimation. Dimmed contrast reduces tracked visual features, mount vibration adds motion blur and persistent pose bias, and frame drops extend intervals of uncorrected dead reckoning. A systematic pose bias can quietly erode the localization allowance without forcing estimated filter covariances or innovation residuals to breach trip thresholds. The release reviewer therefore challenges the combined error against the qualified uncertainty bound, rather than inferring containment from individually passing scalar diagnostics. A breach of the combined bound consumes part of the stopping reserve and invalidates the release warrant; exhausting the entire stopping margin requires a quantified combined-error scenario. Statistical residual monitoring protects against only the specific faults its qualification demonstrates it can detect, leaving site operational restrictions or independent physical checks to cover the remaining biases.

The review also audits the execution integrity of the permission path, verifying whether inference loops or background services can bypass, corrupt, or starve the enforcer (@sec-enforcement) or human overrides (@sec-intervention), the latter covered by claim C6 of @tbl-16-cae-scorecard. Below the proposal boundary (@sec-boundary-machine-model), both safety monitors and manual overrides maintain non-preemptible execution priority over learned models. The reviewer asks concrete systems questions: can a runaway policy thread exhaust shared memory channels, can an accelerator-runtime exception lock a kernel spinlock, or can a telemetry logging burst brown out a regulated power rail? The reviewer accepts **permission path**\index{Permission path} independence—and the held-up power rail that carries it on the mobile manipulator—only after reviewing empirical physical fault-injection trials. These trials must demonstrate resilience under bus saturation, active feed removal, and an abruptly killed proposer task (fault F1), because C2 claims only the faults the permission path demonstrably survives. Those trials must be documented within the signed fault records of @sec-verification-fault-manifest. If the permission path is implemented in user-space software rather than isolated hard real-time threads backed by dedicated hardware interrupt lines, the reviewer marks the safety link as broken.

When an adversarial probe succeeds, the case cannot be salvaged by editing claim descriptions or inserting arbitrary safety margins. The broken warrant is traced to its root systems failure—an uncharacterized physical boundary, an inadequate dataset, or an unmodeled bus latency—and the defect returns to the owning engineering subsystem. For example, a motor-current observer that fails under gearbox compliance returns to the mechanical specification as wear limits and runtime compliance estimation, while bus contention that delays the enforcer returns to the compute architecture as memory partitioning and real-time scheduling. The case returns to the engineering team with its broken warrants named, and only updated boundaries, re-derived stopping distances, and renewed verification reopen formal adjudication.

Adversarial review must also recur periodically, because a case accepted once can erode in service without any single discrete event forcing a new audit. The *normalization of deviance*\index{Normalization of deviance} names that operational erosion, in which anomalies that cause no immediate harm come to be treated as acceptable operating noise rather than as evidence against a warrant [@leveson2011engineering; @vaughan1996challenger] (\ref{ws-release-challenger-experience-base-as-boundary}).[^fn-deviance-normalization-origin] On the mobile manipulator, this erosion unfolds silently across months of fleet operation: localization residuals creep toward the edge of their tolerance, observation-age watchdog trips are dismissed as nuisance stops, stopping distances end slightly longer than the initial trials did, and enforcer trips are cleared on the floor without a trace review. When thresholds are widened, margins trimmed for throughput, and alarms suppressed because nothing has yet gone wrong, the gap between the signed envelope and the machine's actual physical behavior widens until a routine disturbance exhausts what remains.

[^fn-deviance-normalization-origin]: **Normalization of Deviance**\index{Normalization of deviance!origin}: The sociologist Diane Vaughan coined the term in her study of the Challenger launch decision [@vaughan1996challenger]. It names a process rather than a decision, in which each anomaly that caused no harm widened what the next review accepted as normal. The countermeasure is therefore an indicator with a threshold fixed in advance, which a run of harmless readings cannot move.

::: {#ws-release-challenger-experience-base-as-boundary .callout-war-story title="Challenger and experience limits (1986)"}
**Context**: The Space Shuttle's solid rocket motors were assembled from cylindrical steel segments whose field joints were sealed by primary and secondary O-rings [@rogers1986challenger]. No learned model appears in this chain. The adjudication failure it records is the exact failure this chapter's verdicts exist to prevent: a launch approved for conditions that the evidence did not cover.

**Mechanism**: The ambient temperature at launch was $36^\circ\text{F}$, 15 degrees colder than any previous launch. O-ring resiliency falls with temperature, and a cold ring returns to shape too slowly to follow the joint gap as ignition pressure opens it. On the eve of launch, engineers at Morton Thiokol, the motor's contractor, recommended against launching below $53^\circ\text{F}$, the O-ring temperature of the coldest previous flight, whose joints had shown the worst blow-by to date. That limit was the outer edge of flight experience, not a qualified bound. NASA managers countered with a qualification temperature that applied to the propellant's bulk temperature rather than to the joint seals.

**Impact**: A combustion gas leak through the right booster's aft field joint, beginning at or shortly after ignition, weakened or penetrated the External Tank. The vehicle broke up about 73 seconds after launch, and all seven crew members died.

**Response**: The presidential Commission attributed the failure to "a faulty design unacceptably sensitive to a number of factors," and temperature heads its list of those factors. It recommended that the joint be changed and that the new design be certified by tests "over the full range of operating conditions, including temperature."

**Systems lesson**: Thiokol management reversed its engineers' recommendation at the urging of NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center. Thiokol's vice president of engineering testified, "We had to prove to them that we weren't ready." The burden of proof had inverted: rather than requiring proof that the joint was safe inside its evidence, adjudicators demanded proof that it was unsafe outside the evidence, where no data existed. The Commission also found that O-ring erosion had recurred on earlier flights and that NASA and Thiokol "accepted escalating risk apparently because they 'got away with it last time'" [@rogers1986challenger], so the flight record itself had been read as evidence of safety. A release verdict keeps the burden where the envelope trichotomy puts it. A condition outside the evidence, such as a seal temperature below all flight experience, is unknown, and the verdict refuses it.
:::

The human-takeover premise in the Tempe collision (@sec-boundary-when-fails) was an operational assumption of the exact same kind, raising the critical operator-monitoring questions examined in @sec-intervention-failure-modes. A release case that relies on such a premise must bind its operational response—whether an outright refusal or a restricted case—directly to verified, empirical physical limits.

A case that survives adversarial review has had its warrants aggressively tested, but its verdict still lives only on paper. The release manifest turns the surviving argument and the verdict it supports into an immutable, machine-readable record that the machine itself checks before it moves.
## The Release Manifest {#sec-release-manifest}

A release verdict is formally codified in the **release manifest**\index{Release manifest!definition}\index{Release contract!release manifest}, the fourteenth record in our deployment record chain. This signed, tamper-evident data structure cryptographically binds every upstream engineering contract, the structured argument graph, the operational envelope limits, and live standing conditions to the adjudicator's verdict by cryptographic digest. Rather than relying on static documentation or procedural sign-offs, the manifest binds the Goal Structuring Notation assurance argument and operational design domain invariants directly to their empirical evidence. At the wire level, it serves as the ultimate gating mechanism: the target platform refuses physical motion whenever runtime binary images, silicon attestation measurements, or underlying qualification data diverge from these signed digests.[^fn-hw-crypto-manifest]

The release manifest synthesizes the engineering contracts established throughout this book. Each upstream record defines an operational boundary or contributes empirical data that the overarching safety case must validate; mere existence or signature on an isolated contract does not validate the system as a whole. Instead, the manifest incorporates reviewed snapshots of these records into a coherent argument graph:

1. **Physical plant and timing base:** The kinodynamic limit record (@sec-body-actuator-limits) documents torque, velocity, and thermal dissipation bounds alongside their qualification data; the proposer's payload requirements (@sec-brain-action-chunking) specify candidate action horizons that feed the handoff record rather than standing as an isolated contract; and the handoff record (@sec-nervous-deterministic-fieldbuses) establishes deterministic fieldbus jitter, cycle deadlines, and real-time communication premises.
2. **Data, policy, and behavioral bounds:** The demonstration provenance record (@sec-data-schema) captures dataset calibrations, sensor configurations, and operating-domain coverage; the policy manifest (@sec-training-policy-manifest) binds frozen neural network weights to the empirical behavioral bounds proven for that candidate model; and the evaluation record (@sec-evaluation-logs) details closed-loop task success rates, human intervention tallies, and stress-tested operational conditions.
3. **Perception, belief, and planning:** The observation contract (@sec-perception-observation-contract) enforces observation freshness and multi-sensor synchronization windows; the spatial belief record (@sec-memory-handoff) specifies geometric state estimates, state covariance, and validity domains; the intent lease (@sec-intent-handoff) records task objectives, spatial tolerances, and preemption conditions; and the trajectory record (@sec-planning-trajectory-contract) encodes motion profiles, kinematic seam continuity, execution deadlines, and safe stopping continuations.
4. **Deterministic containment, execution, and verification:** The enforcement record (@sec-enforcement-admitted-command-schema) logs the command stream admitted by runtime safety filters, cleanly separated from the signed enforcement contract that specifies barrier functions and fallback triggers; the placement record (@sec-placement-hardware-allocation) guarantees compute scheduling, memory isolation, and processor affinity; the authority record (@sec-intervention-authority-log) documents arbitration switches and fallback outcomes; and the fault records (@sec-verification-fault-manifest) index tested fault-injection scenarios alongside known coverage gaps.

Beyond linking these upstream contracts, the release manifest contributes its own architectural elements: the root claim, the cryptographic digest of the Goal Structuring Notation argument graph, binary hashes across all deployed software (spanning learned policy weights, the deterministic enforcer logic in both nominal and restricted modes, and the real-time operating system kernel), sensor calibration tables, the adjudicator's digital signature, mandatory standing operational conditions, an accumulated lifecycle wear budget of operating hours and load cycles, and a strict calendar expiration timestamp. All evidence links must resolve to these exact reviewed record digests, organized hierarchically beneath a single evidence root structured as a Merkle hash tree [@merkle1988digital]. Only when the hardware root of trust authenticates this complete cryptographic tree will it permit the motor power stages to energize. While traditional release notes or post hoc compliance certificates summarize safety after the fact, the release manifest operates as an active machine-checked gate: the robot evaluates it before closed-loop control begins, and its runtime monitors revoke motor tracking within a bounded detection-and-response window if any underlying evidence or environmental condition expires.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ **Byte layout:** The release manifest's fields, types, and digests are given in @sec-appendix-systems-wire-release.
:::

[^fn-hw-crypto-manifest]: **Cryptographic Manifest and Silicon Attestation**\index{Cryptographic manifest!hardware Root of Trust}: One-time programmable electronic fuses (OTP/eFuse) store the adjudicator's public verification key in silicon, preventing unauthorized software updates from replacing the root of trust. Secure bootstrap validates each early boot stage before handing over execution control [@arbaugh1997secure], while measured boot extends cryptographic measurements into Trusted Platform Module Platform Configuration Registers (TPM PCRs). The hardware verifier checks these measurements against the digests specified in the signed manifest; any unsigned or modified binary image fails attestation and never receives an operational permit.

@Fig-16-release-record illustrates how authentication and physical standing checks govern the operating permit. The release gate authenticates the manifest, binary images, and complete fault ledger before verifying current sensor calibration, mechanical maintenance thresholds, and operational design domain conditions. Only an exact cryptographic and physical match enables the plant's certified startup sequence; the complete authorization protocol and canonical wire fields appear in @sec-appendix-systems-release-protocol and @sec-appendix-systems-wire-release. During active motion, any breached condition commands an assessed safe fallback before initiating a power bank change or electrical isolation.

::: {#fig-16-release-record fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Fail-closed release pipeline**: The signed verdict and evidence root pass key, image, and complete fault-record authentication, then current calibration, brake, and operating-envelope checks. Every failure path ends in REFUSE. A valid case reaches UNCOND or COND according to what was signed, and stale calibration reaches COND only through a separately signed restricted case; either way, each proposed action is still checked by the permission path. Attribution: Textbook production team (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)." fig-alt="Left-to-right release path: signed release case, authentication of key chain, images, and fault records, then a check of physical standing. Failed authentication, a false or unknown premise, or stale calibration without a separately signed COND case lead down to a REFUSE bar with permit off and an assessed stop or hold. All valid and current checks lead to a COND box for a signed restricted envelope or an UNCOND box for the full envelope; stale calibration covered by a separately signed COND case also leads to the COND box."}
![](images/svg/fig16_release_record.svg){width="100%" fig-alt="Left-to-right release path: signed release case, authentication of key chain, images, and fault records, then a check of physical standing. Failed authentication, a false or unknown premise, or stale calibration without a separately signed COND case lead down to a REFUSE bar with permit off and an assessed stop or hold. \Needspace{22\baselineskip}

| Signed case              | Evidence and standing checks                                                              | Restricted case covering stale calibration | Gate result                                       |
|:-------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `UNCOND`                 | All valid and current                                                                     | Not needed                                 | Full *proposal* envelope under enforcer; `UNCOND` |
| `COND`                   | All restricted evidence valid and current                                                 | Included if calibration stale              | Signed restricted envelope under enforcer; `COND` |
| `UNCOND` or `COND`       | Fault-ledger root/signature mismatch, expiry, image mismatch, or unknown physical premise | Any                                        | Permit off; `REFUSE`                              |
| `UNCOND`                 | Calibration stale                                                                         | No                                         | Permit off; `REFUSE`                              |
| Separately signed `COND` | Only the named calibration is stale; restricted evidence and limits valid                 | Yes                                        | Restricted envelope; `COND`                       |
| `REFUSE`                 | Any                                                                                       | Any                                        | Permit off; `REFUSE`                              |

: **Release authorization truth table**: A restricted mode is a distinct authenticated claim, never an unsigned downgrade of the full case. {#tbl-16-release-authorization}

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ **Protocol:** The gate's step-by-step authorization protocol is given in @sec-appendix-systems-release-protocol.
:::

Every evidence leaf in the assurance Merkle tree must uniquely identify its raw sensor trace, instrumentation hardware, calibration log, machine configuration, and automated test harness script. Measured latency profiles enter the safety case as explicit empirical percentiles, whereas deterministic real-time execution guarantees demand the analytically justified upper bounds derived in @sec-nervous-deterministic-fieldbuses. Similarly, collaborative object-handover criteria require empirical load-cell time series recorded against standardized anthropomorphic surrogates across specified contact geometries. By cryptographically anchoring these primary records, an independent auditor or verification engine can reproduce the experimental test suite and pinpoint the exact operational boundaries where each safety claim ceases to hold.

The release manifest explicitly bounds the physical envelope and hardware configuration under which its verdict remains valid. Modifying a neural policy checkpoint, altering a real-time thread priority, updating a device driver, or replacing an actuator with an unverified component revision immediately invalidates the manifest, demanding a re-adjudicated safety case. In our warehouse mobile manipulator, for example, the manifest enforces signed wear thresholds on harmonic-drive backlash and electromagnetic brake lining thickness derived from empirical stopping-distance and payload trials. Operating envelope tripwires immediately trigger refusal: on-board load cells detect tote-rack overloading beyond rated payload capacity, while facility procedures prevent operation on unmapped or unsurveyed floor surfaces (@tbl-16-odd-invariants). Furthermore, the manifest encodes the isolated, energy-buffered power rail of the permission path (@sec-enforcement-fallback-ladder) as an essential standing invariant, running a diagnostic self-test on the hold-up capacitor bank before granting boot authorization. Whenever a runtime sensor detects that a state variable has breached a signed threshold, the hardware permission path interrupts closed-loop trajectory tracking within its certified detection-and-response deadline and transitions the system into an assessed fallback state.

To maintain physical traceability across time, the manifest must bind all operational telemetry directly to the exact hardware-software revision that generated it. High-resolution local ring buffers capture boundary excursions for post-incident diagnostics, whereas fleet-wide telemetry aggregations reveal systematic mechanical drift across hundreds of operating hours. The curation pipelines examined in @sec-release-data-curation-flywheel must preserve this cryptographic lineage whenever field data is promoted to support a subsequent release case.

During daily operation, edge telemetry logs motor torque residuals, control-loop cycle times, and safety enforcer interventions for trend analysis, while the hardware permission path continuously monitors physical invariants at the multi-kilohertz cadence demanded by the dynamics of the plant. If a routine maintenance check measures brake stopping latency exceeding the signed clearance margin, or if a camera calibration certificate expires, the release verdict is automatically revoked. Re-flashing an older firmware image cannot compensate for worn mechanical friction pads. Unless an engineer deploys a separately signed restricted case (`COND`) that explicitly accommodates that degraded physical state, the controller executes an assessed emergency stop and locks out autonomous motion until certified maintenance and formal re-adjudication take place (@tbl-16-release-authorization).

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The premises a release manifest leaves open become entries in the residual-claims register of @sec-frontier-residual-claims-register.
:::

The warehouse mobile manipulator can safely reach a quiescent state simply by cutting power and engaging mechanical brakes with its base resting stably on the floor. For other robotic morphologies, however, abruptly severing motor power introduces catastrophic instability, as shown by systems that collapse under gravity when torque is removed (\ref{capstone-release-humanoid-crucible}).

::: {#capstone-release-humanoid-crucible .callout-perspective title="When removing torque causes the harm"}
**Question**: Which verdict applies when removing torque causes the harm?

A supported wheeled base at rest eliminates its translational kinetic hazard. In contrast, an upright bipedal humanoid retains substantial gravitational potential energy. While resting in a support gantry before standing up, a `REFUSE` verdict safely holds the robot in its mechanically supported state. Once balanced upright, however, revoking locomotion authority cannot simply de-energize the actuators without inducing an immediate dynamic fall; safe shutdown requires an active, validated arrest or controlled descent strategy.

* **Torque removal can cause a fall.** An unsupported biped with backdrivable transmissions will collapse if motor currents drop to zero (@sec-nervous-actuation-authority). Consequently, such physical plants cannot treat torque removal as a fail-safe stopping condition unless accompanied by certified passive catches, lock-up brakes, or an external tether.
* **The fall-arrest response is itself an actuation.** Executing a controlled squat, brace, or step-down to bring the robot to rest is itself an active trajectory that requires validated sensorimotor claims, verified timing margins, and fault-tolerance guarantees. In this regime, executing a safe `REFUSE` action depends on the very control systems maintaining upright stability.
* **Wear revokes the running permit.** Degradation in foot-sole rubber traction or increased backlash in planetary gearheads alters the dynamic margin required for emergency balancing. When telemetry signals that physical wear has crossed the threshold certified in the assurance case, the runtime supervisor must revoke high-speed dynamic locomotion well before the safety-critical arrest maneuvers degrade below their qualifying safety margins.
:::

::: {#chk-release-student-verdict .callout-checkpoint title="Deriving a verdict from your own measurements"}

Notice that @Tbl-16-cond-measurements leaves raw measurement columns empty, reflecting the fact that an engineering textbook provides principles rather than empirical site certifications. Populate this table with empirical data from hardware trials on your own robotic platform, or construct an illustrative benchmark scenario, and evaluate the resulting release verdict:

- [ ] **Graded values**: For each row, record your value and its source, and grade the premise as measured, datasheet, illustrative, or unknown. A user-chosen value grades as illustrative, and a manufacturer's rated value grades as datasheet; measured denotes your own physical trial or a published experimental measurement you cite.
- [ ] **Verdict derivation**: A `COND` case requires adequate support for every relied-on premise: qualified measurements, justified analysis, or validated operating restrictions. Illustrative values alone still support only an actual `REFUSE`. Recompute the base's budget and spare margin from your values. If every relied-on premise has adequate support, name the envelope the `COND` case signs and the premise that keeps the normal mode unsigned. If a relied-on premise lacks adequate support, derive the verdict the table *would* support given the missing evidence, and label that verdict hypothetical.
- [ ] **Artifact label**: Mark the filled table as your own work, whose values license no physical machine.
:::

A release manifest formally bounds and certifies an explicit, immutable system configuration. Any subsequent modification—whether retraining a neural perception head, tightening an actuator torque limit, or swapping a camera lens—invalidates that closure and reopens the underlying safety claims. Sustaining trustworthy autonomy across the operational lifecycle therefore demands that deployment pipelines continuously enforce this rigorous cryptographic chain between empirical evidence, formal assurance arguments, and real-time physical actuation authority.
## Maintaining Release Through Updates {#sec-release-deployment-lifecycle}

Continuing the stipulated warehouse branch, suppose the mobile manipulator's restricted mug-delivery policy is retrained to reduce hesitation at the controlled pick station. Before that candidate neural policy can issue commands to physical actuators, it must pass back through the formal release decision. A signed safety case establishes exactly which historical evidence remains valid, which hardware-in-the-loop tests require re-execution, and how the machine maintains deterministic physical containment throughout the update. Modern deployment mechanisms enforce this decision by protecting the currently validated configuration against runtime corruption and systematically gathering qualification evidence for the candidate.

### Modular safety cases and continuous over-the-air deployment {#sec-release-modular-safety-cases}

Retraining a policy directly alters capability evidence. Yet neural modifications frequently introduce side effects across the shared hardware platform: increased neural accelerator memory bus traffic, altered sensor frame processing latency, or modified contact force trajectories. An engineer must trace these cross-subsystem dependencies before determining which containment records remain valid. While **over-the-air (OTA) updates**\index{Over-the-air update!safety case decomposition}\index{Modular safety case!continuous deployment} swap out a named software payload, **modular safety cases**\index{Safety case!modular GSN decomposition} isolate dependencies by explicitly recording how each claim relies on specific evidence items and platform assumptions [@denney2015dynamic]. Whenever an update alters an underlying dependency, the modular case isolates precisely which safety claims are reopened.

The containment argument provides the rigorous defense against physical harm. It binds together the empirical plant model, physical sensor limits, worst-case execution budgets, and the independent permission path. Key engineering premises include the bounded tracking error tube $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$ (@sec-enforcement-handoff), the emergency stopping budget (@sec-nervous-coupled-budget), the passivity barrier for physical contact (@sec-enforcement-intentional-contact), and hardware watchdog timing margins. Historical verification records for these containment claims remain valid only if the proposed update preserves the exact operating conditions under which they were measured. For example, replacing a backbone network with a higher-capacity model can increase memory bus contention or cause voltage droop on the power rail even if the deterministic safety-filter binary remains byte-for-byte identical. An unchanged enforcer binary does not imply an unchanged containment argument; its guarantees remain bounded by the validated dynamic envelope $\mathcal{C}_{\text{viable}}$ and the system-level timing margins established during qualification.

In parallel, the capability argument demonstrates that the robot reliably fulfills its operational mission within its certified operational design domain. Candidate benchmarking, passive shadow traces, and geofenced closed-loop trials evaluate whether a retrained policy reduces hesitation or improves task throughput. While the low-level enforcer can continuously clamp or reject invalid control proposals to maintain safety, an enforcer that constantly intervenes degrades the robot into an unusable, halting machine. Release engineering therefore evaluates capability and containment as an integrated whole: an update qualifies for fleet dispatch only when the candidate configuration delivers acceptable task performance without undermining the empirical premises supporting its containment envelope.

Modern physical AI platforms maintain configuration integrity during deployment through **dual A/B OS partitioning**\index{Dual A/B OS partitioning!OTA architecture}\index{Atomic update!operating system}. The update agent streams the candidate image onto the inactive storage bank (Bank B) while the incumbent controller continues executing from the active bank (Bank A). Activating the newly flashed partition requires establishing an assessed stationary update state. The physical robot must be safely parked with its payload fully supported, battery reserves must comfortably exceed the threshold needed for re-flashing and post-boot self-tests, and the independent safety supervisor must hold all motor drives in an unpowered or mechanically locked state to prohibit motion during bootloader cutover. The runtime decision to commit or abort this cutover is governed by hardware watchdogs (@sec-release-verdicts-ota-watchdogs). Furthermore, trusting a single fleetwide cryptographic key invites catastrophic compromise: if an attacker extracts that key from one compromised endpoint, they can sign arbitrary firmware for every robot in the field. Robust update architectures mitigate this threat by adopting role-separated signing structures where distinct root, targets, and release keys reside on separate, hardware-isolated infrastructure. The Update Framework (TUF) pioneered this design, and Uptane extended it specifically to automotive and robotics environments where heterogeneous electronic control units require independently authenticated firmware images [@samuel2010survivable; @kuppusamy2016uptane].

Overwriting firmware must never inadvertently destroy the physical calibration history of an individual robot. **Persistent hardware calibration parameter retention**\index{Hardware calibration!persistent parameter retention}\index{Parameter partition!decoupled storage} isolates machine-specific empirical measurements from generic operating system binaries, preventing the dangerous **calibration clashing failure**\index{Calibration clashing failure}. Camera intrinsic matrices ($K$), extrinsic sensor transformations ($[R \mid t]$), kinematic joint zero-point offsets, and motor torque constants ($K_\tau$) reflect the unique mechanical and electrical realities of an individual machine; they drift over time due to mechanical vibration, thermal cycling, and structural wear. Storing these values in a dedicated, wear-leveled, non-volatile parameter partition ensures that flashing an OS image leaves calibration intact. When a firmware update introduces a revised parameter schema, the migration utility writes the transformed schema into a new record while preserving the backward-compatible legacy block, enabling seamless rollback to the prior image-parameter pair. Cryptographic checksums verify the bit-level integrity of these stored calibration blocks, but field release procedures still require physical self-test sanity checks to verify that the stored calibration parameters continue to match physical reality.

Finally, **forensic traceability**\index{Forensic traceability!release provenance}\index{Release manifest!cryptographic provenance} links every running OS image, policy checkpoint, and calibration partition directly to its training provenance, compiler flags, and reviewed HIL regression records via a cryptographically signed release manifest (@sec-release-manifest). When an unexpected field intervention or trajectory excursion occurs, these immutable links enable incident investigators to reconstruct the exact configuration running at that millisecond and determine which safety warrants require re-examination. While a cryptographic digest confirms identity, isolating the physical root cause requires detailed sensor traces and causal analysis.

### Staging candidate policies before release {#sec-release-candidate-staging}

A candidate must repeat the **hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) regression gates**\index{Hardware-in-the-loop!regression gates}\index{Release engineering!HIL regression testing} affected by its changes. While software simulation models timing and electrical behavior only to the fidelity of its mathematical approximations, a physical hardware-in-the-loop test bench exercises the actual microprocessors, interconnect buses, and motor drive electronics under full thermal and electrical load. The bench must rigorously evaluate the specific interference and fault mechanisms on which release claims depend:

1. **Worst-case execution time (WCET) and scheduling jitter**: Profiling whether neural forward passes and safety filter evaluations complete within hard real-time deadlines ($T_{\text{exec}} \le T_{\text{deadline}}$) under peak memory bus crossbar contention and simultaneous DMA transfers (@sec-placement-isolation-decisions).
2. **Deterministic bus arbitration**: Measuring fieldbus communication jitter and cyclic transmission integrity across physical EtherCAT or CAN FD networks under simulated telemetry broadcast floods and electrical noise injection.
3. **Power-stage thermal dynamics and current ripple**: Verifying that high-frequency control chatter or torque ripple proposed by the candidate policy does not induce excessive inverter switching losses, DC rail voltage sag, or thermal runaway in motor windings (@sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles).
4. **Hardware fault-injection survivability**: Validating that physical line breaks, power supply brownouts, or deserializer frame dropouts deterministically trigger the hardware watchdog and safe-stop sequence within certified timing budgets before motor power stages can be damaged.

A candidate policy advances through staging only when every required regression test passes and empirical records confirm that timing and physical margins remain intact. Observing zero deadline overruns during a finite test campaign does not by itself establish a mathematical upper bound on worst-case execution time.

In cloud software engineering, blue-green deployment achieves zero downtime by spinning up an identical green cluster and instantly flipping a virtual IP or DNS CNAME record. In physical AI, however, blue-green cutover cannot be executed instantaneously while mass is in motion. Swapping active control authority between an incumbent controller and a candidate policy mid-stride or at speed requires managing actuator state continuity, motor winding back-EMF, and dynamic tracking tubes (@sec-intervention-authority-transitions); de-energizing motor windings or inducing sudden torque steps introduces severe mechanical shock loads ($N^2 J \ddot{\theta}$) and loss of traction. An unvalidated policy also cannot simply be granted partial motor authority in a populated warehouse to "canary test" edge-case performance.

Safe predeployment staging instead relies on **shadow mode deployment**\index{Shadow mode deployment!definition}. The incumbent controller $\pi_{\text{incumbent}}$ supplies proposals, while the independent enforcer retains sole actuator-output ownership and checks each command before fieldbus dispatch. Concurrently in the background, the candidate neural policy $\pi_{\text{candidate}}$ executes on the host compute SoC, consuming identical live sensor streams $s_t$ within its qualified shared-resource budget and computing what control command $u_t^{\text{cand}} \sim \pi_{\text{candidate}}(s_t)$ it would have proposed. The candidate writes its outputs to an isolated telemetry buffer that grants no actuator authority. Consumers can read that record, but neither the buffer nor the candidate can bypass the enforcer. Shadow inference and recording must stay within the interference and power budgets that preserve the active case. Discrepancies between candidate proposals and the incumbent's admitted commands are logged as high-rate telemetry events without admitting any candidate command to the drives.

Shadow-mode telemetry monitors two instantaneous divergence metrics:

1. **Action discrepancy** ($\Delta u_t$): The Euclidean or angular distance between the candidate proposal and the incumbent control action:
   $$\Delta u_t = \| u_t^{\text{cand}} - u_t^{\text{incumbent}} \|_2.$$
   Sustained spikes in $\Delta u_t$ identify behavioral divergence where the candidate policy exhibits unmodeled bias, high-frequency control jitter, or erratic steering commands. In addition, the discrepancy analyzer monitors the command-rate norm $\|\dot{u}_t^{\text{cand}}\|_2$, which is a torque-rate norm only when $u$ is a torque command, to detect unmodeled control chatter that would excite mechanical resonances.

2. **Safety barrier margin discrepancy** ($\Delta B_t$): The differential proximity to forward-invariant safety boundaries under a control barrier function $h(x)$ (@sec-enforcement-safe-sets-conditional-permission):
   $$\Delta B_t = \dot{h}(\hat{x}_t, u_t^{\text{cand}}) - \dot{h}(\hat{x}_t, u_t^{\text{incumbent}}),$$
   where $\hat{x}_t$ is the state estimated from the sensor streams $s_t$.
   A negative $\Delta B_t$ means the candidate has a smaller modeled barrier derivative than the incumbent. Both derivatives can still be positive, so the sign alone does not imply decreasing clearance or a violated boundary of $\mathcal{C}_{\text{viable}}$ (defined by $h(x) \ge 0$).

The two discrepancies answer different questions. A large $\Delta u_t$ can reflect an alternate useful action, while $\Delta B_t$ indicates how the proposals differ in their modeled effect on the barrier. Neither sign alone supplies a verdict: review must consider the current margin, uncertainty, and the condition that the independent enforcer would require.

Shadow mode nevertheless meets a limit that more traces cannot remove, **counterfactual divergence**\index{Counterfactual divergence!shadow mode}\index{Covariate shift!open-loop replay}. Because admitted incumbent proposals determine the plant trajectory, the historical state trajectory $\tau = (s_0, u_0^{\text{inc}}, s_1, u_1^{\text{inc}}, \dots)$ is conditioned entirely on incumbent actions. The candidate policy operates open-loop; its proposed actions $u_t^{\text{cand}}$ never alter the physical environment, induce vehicle motion, or trigger real-time sensor feedback. Conflating open-loop agreement with deployment safety is the **open-loop replay fallacy**\index{Open-loop replay fallacy}: assuming that high action agreement during passive trace replay guarantees closed-loop dynamic stability. The $O(T^2 \epsilon)$ result in @sec-data-endogenous-experience is an expected-cost bound under its stated imitation-learning assumptions, not a universal law for physical tracking error. A candidate that agrees on incumbent trajectories can still visit unfamiliar states or excite unmodeled dynamics when it closes the loop, the covariate shift that interactive imitation learning was designed to correct [@ross2011reduction]. Shadow mode is an essential pre-filter for gross behavioral anomalies, but never a substitute for closed-loop dynamic qualification.

**Phased canary fleet rollouts**\index{Canary deployment!physical AI fleet}\index{Release engineering!canary rollouts}[^fn-canary-miners-origin] expose the candidate to closed-loop operation under a separately supported restricted case. Selecting fewer machines limits exposure but does not bound the consequence of any one action. The restrictions must address the physical hazard:

1. **Geofenced operational containment**: Canary units operate exclusively within dedicated, surveyed low-risk corridors, such as wide transit aisles devoid of blind rack corners, reduced pedestrian density, and high-friction surveyed concrete ($\mu \ge$ `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_dry_str`).
2. **Enforced kinematic derating**: The real-time safety enforcer clamps candidate policy velocity and acceleration below nominal ratings ($v \le v_{\text{canary}} < v_{\text{nominal}}$), expanding stopping distance margins and suppressing transient kinetic energy.
3. **Supervised human oversight**: High-readiness human supervisors equipped with wireless remote emergency-stop (tele-stop) pendants maintain line-of-sight monitoring over canary units, backed by an active-lease watchdog.
4. **Targeted regression observability**: The trial measures tracking error variance $\sigma_{\text{track}}^2$, drive torque ripple, and enforcer intervention frequency to reveal service regressions. The permission path retains only the containment claims validated for the restricted envelope.

[^fn-canary-miners-origin]: **Canary**\index{Canary deployment!etymology} (the miners' sentinel bird): Miners carried caged canaries because the birds succumb to carbon monoxide before people do, so a bird's distress warned the crew to leave. The metaphor carries this section's warning. The canary is the unit exposed to the hazard first, so on a physical fleet its exposure must be bounded by containment, not by how few units are chosen.

Expansion requires predeclared acceptance criteria tied to the service and physical claims. Intervention-rate non-inferiority,[^fn-noninferiority-canary-margin] with a margin $\delta$ fixed before the trial so that the upper one-sided 95 percent confidence bound on the rate ratio $\lambda_{\text{canary}}/\lambda_{\text{incumbent}}$ must fall below $1+\delta$, and tracking variance $\sigma_{\text{track}}^2 \le \sigma_{\text{incumbent}}^2$ are possible capability criteria, with their comparison conditions and statistical assumptions stated. Without the margin, the criterion becomes a demand to prove the candidate better, which the small exposure of a canary can almost never satisfy; the exposure arithmetic of @sec-evaluation-trial-limits sets how much operation a given $\delta$ requires, and a sequential test (@sec-evaluation-sequential-sprt) can stop expansion as soon as the evidence suffices. None of these criteria replaces the evidence for stopping, observation, or containment. An enforcer intervention also needs causal review: suppressing legitimate clamps to improve a rollout metric would weaken the release argument.

[^fn-noninferiority-canary-margin]: **Non-Inferiority Testing**\index{Non-inferiority test!canary rollout}: The design comes from clinical trials, where failing to find a difference proves nothing, so a new treatment must instead be shown worse than the standard by no more than a margin fixed before any data arrive [@blackwelder1982proving]. A canary can therefore pass on modest exposure without proving the candidate better, but only if $\delta$ was not chosen after the result was seen.

### From qualification to a new manifest {#sec-release-ota-staging}

For the retrained mug-delivery candidate, the reviewer repeats closed-loop capability evaluation under the restricted route and feed conditions, and repeats the loaded timing and fault tests whose dependencies changed. Unaffected plant evidence remains reusable only while configuration, calibration, wear, and site premises still match. A reduced hesitation rate does not justify relaxing contact or floor restrictions.

Assume, still within the stipulated branch, that those results satisfy the predeclared capability criteria and preserve the containment claims. The adjudicator issues a new manifest binding the candidate, retained and repeated evidence, current calibration, and the same restricted mission. At the assessed stationary cutover state, the gate authenticates that manifest and checks current standing conditions before admitting new proposals. Field monitoring then compares the running service with the same success, cycle-time, rescue, and protection criteria. Failed qualification leaves the incumbent case unchanged; a failed standing condition withdraws the affected grant.

### Over-the-air staging and watchdog-enforced rollbacks {#sec-release-verdicts-ota-watchdogs}

A candidate written to the inactive bank inherits no operating grant from its predecessor. **Hardware watchdog rollback triggers**\index{Watchdog rollback!hardware triggers}\index{Hardware watchdog!OTA rollback} must distinguish failure to boot from failure during motion. Before tracking is enabled, failed image authentication, startup tests, or fieldbus synchronization can reject the candidate and select the retained image. That image must still pass current calibration and standing-condition checks; rollback cannot repair the physical plant.

During motion, the independent supervisor first commands the assessed fallback within its measured response budget. Where that response ends in torque removal, the supervisor asserts Safe Torque Off after the required controlled stop; a plant needing a powered hold retains the authority needed for that hold. A missed enforcer heartbeat therefore withdraws tracking permission without making software restart the stopping mechanism. Only after the plant reaches its validated update state may the boot selector change banks.

The image and its compatible calibration schema form the rollback unit. If either record is missing, corrupted, or physically stale, the gate selects `REFUSE` unless a separately signed restricted case covers the actual state and its limits, such as $v \le v_{\text{restricted}}$. Retaining the prior binary image provides an immediate rollback target, but operators must re-validate standing physical conditions before granting that recovered binary active tracking authority.

### Fleet telematics and the closed-loop data curation flywheel {#sec-release-data-curation-flywheel}

An enforcer trip can reveal a policy failure, a changed physical premise, or both. The field record must let the reviewer distinguish those causes before choosing retraining, maintenance, or a narrower envelope. Wireless summaries alone cannot reconstruct the observations and actuator response around the event, so detailed traces are retained locally.

**Edge event-triggered telemetry**\index{Edge event-triggered telemetry!architecture} retains the sensor, proposal, permission, actuator, and timestamp chain around an intervention or boundary excursion. A local rolling buffer preserves the lead-up; capture continues through the physical response when the qualified recording power path survives. Buffer length, write bandwidth, and hold-up energy are sized from the required reconstruction window and verified under the same contention and power faults as the permission path. A logic-rail capacitor does not guarantee that the full sensor and storage path survives, and recording must never delay the stop.

UL 4600 calls the field measurements that keep a claim alive **safety performance indicators**\index{Safety performance indicator} (SPIs). Each is a metric tied to a named claim, with a threshold and a predeclared response when the threshold is crossed [@ul4600]. On the running machine, every standing condition of @sec-release-standing-conditions has one. Measured stop distance at scheduled trials and enforcer trips per operating hour watch the base's stopping claim, age refusals per operating hour watch the observation-age claim, and localization residuals against their allowance watch the sensor geometry. An SPI whose threshold is crossed withdraws or narrows the grant it watches; one that drifts toward its threshold triggers review before it is crossed, which is the defense against the normalization of deviance of @sec-release-adversarial-review.

Compact health summaries support fleet monitoring, while required incident records retain full provenance locally until transfer succeeds. Learning-data filters may prioritize unfamiliar events, but cannot discard required safety evidence or hide repeated failures. A reviewer distinguishes policy hesitation from calibration drift, contamination, and mechanism wear before assigning the repair. Qualified recovery traces can enter the experience pipeline of @sec-data-schema; reconstructed simulations extend test coverage only over their modeled conditions.

A captured event changes the release argument only after its cause and conditions are established. Reconstructed scenes and retraining can improve a candidate, but neither automatically repairs a physical warrant. The revised claim must return through the relevant qualification stages before a new manifest grants authority.

### Recorded people as a standing condition {#sec-release-recorded-people}

Every record this release relies on also records people. The authority log of @sec-intervention-authority-log names the operator behind each takeover, tick by tick. The event-triggered traces above hold camera frames of whoever stood in the aisle, workers who never touched the console among them, and the demonstration archive of @sec-data-schema binds each episode to the operator who produced it. None of that evidence can be discarded without weakening the incident reconstruction that the release depends on, and none of it is only about the machine. The release therefore carries one more premise, and it is administrative rather than physical: each record that identifies a person declares its purpose, its retention period, and who may read it, and the site operates within those declarations.

Where the machine runs in the European Union, the General Data Protection Regulation makes that premise law [@gdpr2016].
